answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond that peers may slash if it attests to fraud. A lone forger, circling like a raven, might spawn a thousand agents, but each one now ties up real capital, and one exposed lie burns the stake of every account that echoed it. Composing a sonnet of fake consensus becomes like emptying an ocean with a cup: the attacker pays for every extra voice, while an honest agent pays once and later reclaims its deposit.
